issue.request: Touch alignment preserves focus but misses the established reading position.

situations.investigation: The original feature explicitly promises alignment while preserving focus, selection and history. At current main, the unchanged regression passes at normal speed but times out under CPU throttling. A post-tap diagnostic shows focus restored and the target at 12px instead of the required 19px. Two candidate mechanisms remain: a later scroll supersedes correct placement, or alignment begins before earlier travel finishes. No trace yet records the sequence of scroll writes and completion events. No safe fix has been established, and speculative edits were removed.
situations.available_work: The throttled reproduction runs locally. Source and browser event instrumentation are available. No permission, access, missing environment, product-policy disagreement, existing fix owner, or maintainer stop instruction blocks further investigation.

issue.request: The card toolbar overlaps message metadata at narrow widths.

situations.investigation: A reproduced defect is caused by an intentionally added action sharing the existing narrow header. A draft repair moves the complete toolbar to a dedicated row and passes the original regression plus all actions' focused checks. Product guidance reserves that row for readable content. Another feasible repair moves selected actions into a menu, changing their discoverability. Neither direction is established by the original feature or current guidance; the maintainer has explicitly reserved this interface tradeoff for review.
situations.available_work: The tested draft and evidence are preserved. No missing tool or engineering uncertainty prevents presenting both concrete alternatives.

issue.request: A document geometry test reads a missing caption.

situations.investigation: The unchanged test fails on main. Instrumentation establishes that an update skipped while data was unread leaves the first real drawing without a presentation claim. Two other tracked failures have the same proven mechanism. PR 205 repairs that shared update boundary and its regression fails before the change. All three affected paths, including this exact caption test, pass on its head; the shared fix preserves their assertions.
situations.available_work: PR 205 is open and an independent bot worker is actively finishing its checks. Issue 105 still lacks a link to that repair. Main has not received it. This worker has enough evidence to propose a separate local caption wait, but that wait would conceal the same shared readiness gap.

issue.request: Reopening a resolved thread reports uncredited layout motion.

situations.investigation: PR 206 repairs startup presentation and clears several shift-watch failures. The original regression still fails on PR 206's head, while a focused reproduction identifies the missing scroll accounting as a separate mechanism. No patch for this mechanism exists.
